gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-17 Keychron's US store lists the K8 Max (ANSI), ChatGPT's 'best practical office' pick shown at $114.99, at $94.99 but marks it unavailable; the same store sells the Q1 Max at $209.99 (list $229.99), while the aluminum Lofree Flow 2 84 is $159 and the plastic Flow Lite 2 84 is $109 at Lofree.
standout_why: I tried to open both cited rival pages: RTINGS 'Best Keyboards For Typing' (rtings.com/keyboard/reviews/best/by-usage/writers) and Tom's Guide 'best mechanical keyboards'. WebFetch returned only site navigation and none of the article text, and downloading them with curl was not permitted, so I could not read their picks or prices. ChatGPT's own answer shows the K8 Max at $114.99 at Keychron and gives only rough figures for the Q1 Max ('$200–$230 typical') and Air75 V3 ('Around $140'). It does not say the K8 Max is unavailable at Keychron today, and it does not price either Lofree. The score is 2, not 3, because I could not confirm the rival pages leave this out.
decides: Two of ChatGPT's four picks have problems at the maker's store today. The K8 Max (ANSI) is marked unavailable there, so its 'practical office' slot can't be filled from Keychron. The Q1 Max is $209.99, which is $50.99 more than the Lofree Flow 2 84 at $159. That makes the Flow 2 84 the cheapest aluminum-case pick on the page I could price at a maker's store. The Flow Lite 2 84 at $109 is now the cheapest maker-priced option, since the K8 Max can't be bought from Keychron. The Logitech MX Mechanical Mini ($159.99) costs within a dollar of the Flow 2 84, and Logitech's product page lists no switch force, travel or hot-swap support.
